item.title: The nation’s largest school districts consider ditching Google Search
item.description:
New York, Los Angeles, and Chicago schools are considering Google alternatives after the company said it will disable Search for schools that opt out of its AI features, according to The New York Times. Starting next year, schools will not have the option to disable Gemini-powered features without also disabling Search. Chris Phillips, Google's vice president of education, told the Times that, "Search and AI are deeply integrated," and that schools that turn off Google's AI features "will not have access to Search."

item.title: Sony’s impressive Bravia 8 II OLED hits a new low price ahead of Black Friday
item.description:
Black Friday is a great time to save on a new OLED television for your winter movie nights. Though, it turns out that you can already get a great deal on the 65-inch Sony Bravia 8 II, one of our favorite OLED televisions. It’s currently discounted by $1,100 at various retailers, including Amazon, Best Buy, and directly from Sony. That discount brings the price under $2,200, the lowest we’ve seen. You can also save $800 on the 55-inch model, which is typically $2,599.99 (Amazon, Best Buy, Sony), but now costs just under $1,800.

Sony Bravia 8 II OLED TV

The Bravia 8 II was chosen as the “king of TV” by a panel of judges (including The Verge’s own Nilay Patel) in Value Electronics’ 2025 shootout. The OLED TV has excellent color accuracy, a bright panel, and a 120Hz refresh rate.

Where to Buy:

  • $3299.99 $2198 at Amazon (65-inch)
  • $3299.99 $2199.99 at Best Buy (65-inch)
  • $3299.99 $2199.99 at Sony (65-inch)

My colleague John Higgins praised the Bravia 8 II for its excellent image quality and engaging picture, though those positive traits are consistent with almost all OLED TVs. What sets this one apart is its impressive image processing, the bold colors from its quantum dot-equipped OLED panel, and that it looks great right out of the box (although he recommends using Professional mode). The screen was awarded the top spot at 2025’s Value Electronics TV Shootout, beating out similar offerings from competitors like Panasonic, LG, and Samsung.

For gaming, the panel can reach up to 120Hz at 4K, with both variable refresh rate and automatic low-latency mode to ensure that your content looks and feels good to play. The connectivity includes two HDMI 2.1 (one with eARC), and two HDMI 2.0 ports, giving you plenty of inputs for consoles and a Blu-ray player, among other gadgets. We spotted some color fringing of certain colors in dark scenes, and lamented the lack of a but it’s an otherwise excellent screen we can easily recommend.

Read our Sony Bravia 8 II OLED review.

item.title: Instagram now lets you edit your stories after you post them
item.description:
Instagram's latest update will allow you to edit your Stories without losing your views, likes, or replies. You can now edit the text, music, stickers, and drawings for up to 15 minutes after sharing your Story, Instagram head Adam Mosseri has announced.

Reverse engineer Alessandro Paluzzi first spotted Instagram working on this feature in April, but now it's official. Previously, you had to delete and repost your Story to fix a typo or add a song that you forgot to include.

You can edit your post by opening your Story and selecting the three-dot menu in the bottom-right corner. From there …

Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: The leaked Lenovo Legion Go Beam could be the affordable handheld we need
item.description:

item.description:

item.title: The best early Black Friday deals you can already shop
item.description:
The countdown to Black Friday is on, and the discounts are starting to appear. Although the shopping holiday isn’t officially until November 27th, retailers are already dropping early deals on some of our favorite tech. Of course, with prices rising across the board, a good discount doesn’t necessarily mean you’re getting a historically low price. But we’re still seeing worthwhile discounts on a host of tried-and-tested gear, with more expected next week.

Below, we’ve rounded up the best early Black Friday deals we’ve found so far. Prices could drop further as Black Friday approaches, as is always the case, but these deals are worth considering if you’d rather shop early and beat the holiday rush. We’ll continue to update this guide as more retailers launch their holiday sales, too, so be sure to check back regularly as we get closer to the main event.

AirPods Pro 3

Apple’s AirPods Pro 3 deliver the best noise cancellation and sound quality of any AirPods yet, along with a more comfortable, secure fit and improved water resistance. They also feature built-in heart rate tracking for workouts and support live translations for a handful of languages. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

  • $249 $179 at Amazon
  • $249 $179 at Walmart
  • $249 $179.99 at Best Buy

Sony DualSense Wireless Controller

Sony’s DualSense Wireless Controller for the PlayStation 5 features immersive haptic feedback and resistance triggers, which feel great to use. It offers a built-in mic, a 3.5mm headphone jack, and a mute button; it also works with PC, macOS, and mobile devices via Bluetooth or USB-C.

Where to Buy:

  • $74.99 $54 at Amazon
  • $74.99 $54.99 at Best Buy
  • $74.99 $54.99 at Target

007 First Light

007 First Light, a third-person stealth action game from the studio behind Hitman, is arguably the best action game we’ve played this year. It features a wide variety of missions that have you sneaking through enemy territory, engaging in hand-to-hand combat, and taking part in high-speed car chases — you know, classic Bond stuff. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

  • $69.99 $34.99 at PlayStation Store

Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K Plus

Amazon’s last-gen Fire TV Stick 4K Plus streams in 4K and supports Dolby Atmos, Dolby Vision, and Alexa Plus. It also ships with the redesigned Fire OS and, unlike more recent models, still lets you sideload Android TV apps.

Where to Buy:

  • $69.99 $29.99 at Amazon
  • $69.99 $29.99 at Best Buy

Apple Watch Series 12

The Apple Watch Series 12 introduces AI-powered Audio Intelligence features, including sound recognition alerts, Live Rewind, and Siri Recap. It can also track your heart rate every five seconds, even when you’re not exercising, and offers faster charging than prior models. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

  • $399 $329 at Amazon
  • $399 $329 at Walmart
  • $399 $329 at Best Buy

Philips Hue Essential four-pack of bulbs

Philips Hue bulbs can be pricey, which is why the company’s four-pack of Essential A19 bulbs is a great buy at the current sale price. The adjustable bulbs offer white and color ambiance, 800 lumens of brightness, and can be controlled either via Bluetooth or a Hue Bridge (sold separately).

Where to Buy:

  • $59.99 $41.99 at Amazon (four-pack)
  • $119.99 $99.99 at Best Buy (with Hue Bridge)
  • $119.99 $97.99 at Amazon (with Hue Bridge)

Fanttik S1 Pro Cordless Electric Screwdriver

Fanttik’s rechargeable electric screwdriver features three adjustable torque settings, a built-in LED light, and 16 S2 hardened steel bits for tackling everything from furniture assembly to small electronics repairs. It also comes with a magnetic storage case and supports USB-C.

Where to Buy:

  • $79.99 $39.99 at Amazon

Nothing Ear 3A earbuds

You likely won’t find wireless earbuds with a more striking appearance than Nothing’s Ear 3A. They also sound fantastic, boast active noise cancellation, and offer robust EQ settings, making them a great pick for the price. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

  • $99 $69 at Amazon
  • $99 $69 at Walmart
  • $99 $69 at Best Buy

MacBook Neo

Apple’s most affordable laptop uses the same A18 Pro chip found in the iPhone 16 Pro. It features a vibrant 13-inch display, surprisingly good speakers, and 8GB of RAM, making it a solid option for students and anyone who needs a laptop for everyday tasks. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

  • $799 $749 at Amazon (512GB)
  • $699 $649 at Best Buy (256GB)
  • $699 $649 at Amazon (256GB)

Bose SoundLink Max SE speaker

The cheaper, more streamlined SoundLink Max features a slightly smaller battery (16 vs. 20 hours) and lacks external power bank functionality. Otherwise, it’s the same as the standard model, which means the audio is just as great.

Where to Buy:

  • $349 $229 at Best Buy

Ember Mug 3 (14-ounce)

Ember’s latest smart mug is designed to keep your coffee at the ideal temperature for up to three hours, with five temp settings between 120 and 145 degrees Fahrenheit. The third-gen version is similar to prior models; however, you can now adjust the heat settings directly on the mug and throw it in the dishwasher, which wasn’t the case before.

Where to Buy:

  • $149.95 $99.99 at Amazon
  • $149.95 $99.99 at Best Buy
  • $149.95 $99.99 at Ember

Despite being an entry-level variant of the B6 OLED, this model features four HDMI 2.1 ports, a 120Hz refresh rate, a capable processor, and pixel-perfect image quality and contrast for any content you want to watch. Lower brightness is likely the biggest compromise with getting a cheaper OLED.

  • $449.95 $149.95 at Best Buy

Hisense’s 2026 CanvasTV is a 4K QLED TV that doubles as wall art when you’re not watching. It features a matte, anti-glare display and runs on Google’s excellent TV software; it’s also a great pick for gamers thanks to its snappy 144Hz variable refresh rate and a pair of HDMI 2.1 ports.

  • $1499.99 $699.99 at Best Buy (55-inch)

Where to Buy:

Birdfy’s metal smart bird feeder features a wide-angle 4K camera that lets you get an up-close look at visiting birds, along with a 1.8-liter seed capacity and a built-in solar panel for charging. It also offers free AI-powered recognition of more than 6,000 bird species.

Where to Buy:

Tessan’s universal travel adapter delivers up to 205W of combined USB charging power and can charge up to eight devices, including a pair of laptops, at the same time. It features six USB-C ports, including two that can deliver up to 140W individually, a USB-A port, and an AC outlet. It also works in over 200 countries and regions.

Where to Buy:

Bambu Lab P2S Combo

Bambu Lab’s P2S Combo is a 3D printer that can print in multiple colors and automatically dry its materials to help improve print quality. It also features a 5-inch touchscreen, a built-in camera for monitoring prints remotely, and AI-powered tools that can detect printing problems.

Where to Buy:

  • $749 $649 at Bambu Lab

Eight Sleep Pod 6

Eight Sleep’s Pod 6 automatically adjusts your bed’s temperature based on your sleep patterns, heart rate, and breathing. It features a redesigned hub that’s half the size of its predecessor and adjusts temperatures faster. Where to Buy:

  • $2899 $2699 at Eight Sleep

Flextail Zero Pump 2

Flextail’s Zero Pump 2 might weigh a mere 1.7 ounces, but it can quickly inflate and deflate a sleeping pad. It comes with six nozzles and a replaceable battery that recharges via USB-C, allowing you to inflate up to 30 pads on a single charge.

Where to Buy:

  • $56.99 $50.15 at Flextail (with code BF12)

Litter-Robot 4 Starter Bundle

The last-gen Litter-Robot 4 can monitor your cat’s visits, track their weight, and automatically separate waste from clean litter after each use, so you can go up to eight days without emptying your cat’s litter box. The so-called starter bundle also includes 20 pounds of litter, 25 waste drawer liners, a host of odor-control accessories, a litter-trapping mat, and a three-year warranty.

Headspace subscription

Headspace makes it easier to build mindfulness into your everyday life, whether you’re looking to manage stress, improve focus, or get a better night’s sleep. An annual subscription gives you access to hundreds of guided meditations, breathing exercises, and other tools for beginners and experienced users alike.

Casetify Moonaries illo Edition 2 phone case

Part of Casetify’s early Black Friday sale, which offers up to 50 percent off select phone case styles, this Moonaries Illo case features playful artwork from the illustrator behind Mocha Cat. It’s available for the iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone 16 Pro, and other iPhone models.

Sharge Icemag 3 Power Bank

The Icemag 3 can wirelessly deliver up to 25W of power to compatible smartphones and up to 35W wired charging via USB-C. The 10,000mAh Qi2 charger can also act as a foldable kickstand, comes with an integrated USB-C cable that serves as a lanyard, and sports a transparent design with colorful RGB lighting.
